summary: Independent review of the device hash map writer slots and claim on OFD locks (84ce9813d), each finding checked by a refuter

findings.title: A vfork/posix_spawn child's first write opens a description in its own fd table and records it in the parent's table: the parent then writes its slot without the lock, so a seal discounts its live writer and counts wrap
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:389-403 (fast path trusts e->slot), 407-451 (slow path; ensure_description 218 opens in the caller's fd table), 432-433 (exchange to 0), 464-485 (discount), 274-294 (sum compared to 0); plan PLAN-stage1.md:193-197 and :1237
findings.problem: Precondition: a task that shares the process's memory but has its own fd table (vfork child, glibc posix_spawn's CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK child, Python subprocess's vfork child, clone(CLONE_VM) without CLONE_FILES) runs a BPF write on a 1533 map when the process has no description for it yet (its first write, or after a forget). No fork handler runs there. slow_writer_count/ensure_description open the segment file in the child's fd table, take slot s's lock through that new description, and store e->fd and e->slot into local_maps, which is the parent's memory. The child's exec or _exit closes the description and the kernel frees the lock. The parent's fast path (my_writer_count) keeps returning &writers[s].count with no lock behind it, for every later write, for good. A realistic trigger is a host that spawns often, with a program on execve, close or dup2 in libc. There the first write, and often every write, comes from a spawn child, so the parent never holds a lock. Consequences: (a) a sealer in another process finds slot s's lock free, clears the count of the parent's live writer that read PHASE 0, and returns true while that writer still writes the frozen table; (b) the writer's later fetch_sub wraps the count to UINT64_MAX; (c) with no seal involved, another live process takes the free slot and clears the parent's live count (cpp:428-433, logged as 'a process that is gone'), so two live processes then share one slot; (d) a wrapped slot makes the sealer's sum wrap (UINT64_MAX + 1 = 0, cpp:279-282, 290-293), so a well-behaved process's writer in flight is invisible and a seal returns true at once. When the wrapped slot is shared with a live holder R, R's own writer in flight reads that slot as 0. This contradicts plan section 10's slots-8 row ('a vfork child shares its parent's slot (README 10, alive side)') and D8's limits, which put vfork children only on the alive side. No test covers a vfork child.

(exec /bin/true) wrote key 1; its slot 21' / 'lock of slot 21 now: FREE (nobody holds it)' / 'parent writer parked after reading PHASE 0, counting in slot 21 (count 1)' / '[info] ... discounting 1 writer(s) left in flight in slot 21 by a process that is gone' / 'sealer ...: seal_and_build=1, phase=1, key 2 in image=0' / 'parent writer returned 0' / 'slot 21 count after its decrement: 18446744073709551615'. Step 5 of the same run models a D15 rollback (unseal after a failed copy). Process Q writes and parks after reading PHASE 0: 'sum of counts now 0' / 'second sealer: seal_and_build=1, key 3 in image=0 (Q still parked)'. With no seal (usable_slots 1), /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-ofd-review/slots/repro_vfork_share.cpp, output /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-ofd-review/slots/build/out_vfork_share.txt: 'writer slot 0 taken; 1 writer(s) left in flight there by a process that is gone' / 'live process R ... slot 0 lock now HELD by R; count 0 while the parent's writer is still in flight' / 'slot 0 count now 0xffffffffffffffff (two live processes in slot 0)'.
findings.suggested_change: Never let a task that did not run the fork handler open or record a description. Record the pid that owns local_maps (set at load and in devhash_fork_child). In slow_writer_count, claim and still_holds_claim, compare getpid() with it; on a mismatch, return the overflow slot without touching local_maps or local_mutex. The fast path stays as is, since a vfork child that uses the parent's slot is covered by the parent's shared description. Compare each slot with 0 in sealer_enter/sealer_poll instead of their sum, and treat a count above a sane bound as corrupt. Add a test that does the first write in a vfork child and then seals while the parent writes. Correct plan section 10 and D8's limits.

findings.title: The fork handler, the destructor and the generation change close a recorded fd number without checking it is still the segment's description: they close host fds
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:235-236 (devhash_fork_child), 359-360 (~nv_gpu_device_hash_map_impl), 183-184 (local_entry, new map at an old address); contrast 204-206
findings.problem: Once the recorded description is gone, e->fd is only a number, and the host may reuse it for its own file. That happens through the documented host close (close_range, D8 dead side) or through slots-1's vfork child. ensure_description knows this and forgets without closing ('A description the host closed (its number may name another file now) is forgotten, not closed', cpp:204-206). The three other sites call close(e->fd) unconditionally. As a result, every fork child of the host loses the host's file at that number before user code runs (sockets, pipes to workers, logs). The process that destroys the map loses it in the parent. A new map at the old address closes it in any process. This violates the host-safety rules: the host's own fds are closed by the agent.
findings.evidence: Independent of vfork: /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-ofd-review/slots/repro_stalefd.cpp. The host writes (description at fd 3), runs close_range(3, ~0U), opens /dev/null 4 times, writes again, then forks and destroys the map. Output /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-ofd-review/slots/build/out_stalefd.txt: "host's own fds: 3 4 5 6" / 'fork child: host fd 4 CLOSED (fork handler)' / "host: fd 4 CLOSED by the map's destructor". The vfork trigger gives the same result: /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-ofd-review/slots/build/out_vfork_exec.txt (last two lines). A real hang came out of it: in /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-ofd-review/slots/repro_vfork_lowpipe.cpp the test's own pipe got fd 4, the handler closed the write end in the forked child Q, and the parent blocked until timeout. Output /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-ofd-review/slots/build/out_vfork_lowpipe.txt: "Q's pipe: read fd 3, write fd 4" / 'rc=124'.
findings.suggested_change: Before closing e->fd at all three sites, fstat it and compare st_dev/st_ino with e->dev/e->ino, as ensure_description does. Close only on a match; otherwise just forget. Better, keep the description at a high number (see slots-4), so that a stale number rarely names a host file.

findings.title: The documented host-close limit is understated: after close_range every later write runs without a lock, and the owner's own rescan clears its live writers' counts (wrap)
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:389-403 (no re-validation on the fast path), 207-219 (forget, then reopen), 606-614 (still_holds_claim calls ensure_description), 565-575 (claim), 425-433 (rescan from pid % n, exchange to 0); PLAN-stage1.md:198-199
findings.problem: The plan states: 'On the dead side: a host that closes descriptors it does not own (close_range, item 8) releases its slot. A write in flight at that moment can be missing from the device copy.' The code is wider than that. (1) The fast path never re-checks the description, so every write after the close, for the rest of the process's life, counts in a slot whose lock is free. Any seal can discount such a write and return true while it writes, and any other process can take and clear the slot. (2) In the owner process the per-delivery still_holds_claim(), or claim(), runs ensure_description, which forgets the slot (slot = -1) and opens a new description while other threads are in flight on the old slot. The next write rescans from getpid() % n, which is usually the same slot because its lock is now free. That clears the count of this process's own live writers, the log says they belong to 'a process that is gone', and their decrements then wrap the count to UINT64_MAX. Through the sum-wrap in slots-1 (d), that wrapped slot later hides another process's writer from a seal. The README and plan limit says none of this.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-ofd-review/slots/repro_close.cpp, output /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-ofd-review/slots/build/out_close.txt. Part 1: 'host ran close_range(3, ~0U); now 300 ms of nothing' / 'a write 300 ms after the close parked after reading PHASE 0, in slot 73' / '... discounting 1 writer(s) left in flight in slot 73 by a process that is gone' / 'sealer: seal_and_build=1, key 2 in image=0' / 'the writer returned 0; slot 73 count now 0xffffffffffffffff'. Part 2 (owner): '[warning] ... description of the segment was closed' / '[info] ... writer slot 73 taken; 1 writer(s) left in flight there by a process that is gone' / 'owner=1, still_holds_claim=0; thread 1 in flight in slot 73, count after the rescan 0' / "after thread 1's decrement, slot 73 count 0xffffffffffffffff".
findings.suggested_change: When ensure_description finds the description gone, remember the old slot as tainted: never take it again in this process and never exchange its count. Re-validate the description cheaply on the writer path at a bounded rate, for example an fstat at most every 100 ms through the slow path as the overflow retry does, so that exposure is bounded. State the remaining limit in D8 and the README: every write until the re-check, and the wrap that follows if the slot is cleared under live writers.

findings.title: The lazily opened description takes the lowest free fd: in a host started with two of fds 0-2 closed it becomes stderr/stdout, and the host's writes land in the segment's header
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:70 and 91 (fopen of /proc/self/maps, then open(path, O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC)), 218 (ensure_description at a process's first write), 659 (seal's probe description)
findings.problem: This commit is the first to keep a long-lived fd open on the segment file. It is opened at the first write of each map, at any point in the host's life, not at load time. Neither open is moved above 2. When two of fds 0-2 are free (a daemon or a run with '>&- 2>&-' or '<&- >&-'), fopen takes the first free one and the segment file the next. The host's next write to that std stream (perror, a log line, printf) goes into the shared segment's file through an O_RDWR description at offset 0, which overwrites the managed segment's header. Every process that maps the segment can then fault. The sealer's per-seal probe description (cpp:659) has the same exposure while it is open. This breaks the rule to leave the host's standard streams untouched.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-ofd-review/slots/repro_stdio.cpp closes fds 1 and 2, does one map write, then write(2, 'host: something went wrong'). Output /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-ofd-review/slots/build/out_stdio.txt: 'fd 2 is now: /dev/shm/devhash-slots-stdio-4183627' / 'host write(2) returned 27' / 'segment file bytes 0..15 before: 02 00 00 00 ...' / 'after:  68 6f 73 74 3a 20 73 6f 6d 65 74 68 69 6e 67 20 ("host: something ")'.
findings.suggested_change: Right after opening, move both descriptions to a high number with fcntl(fd, F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, N), N for example 100 or above, then close the low one. Read /proc/self/maps with open+read rather than fopen, or check that no fd at or below 2 is left in use. Do the same for the probe in seal().

findings.title: Plan D8 and the code disagree on the lock bytes and on the segment-file fallback
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:381-387 (lock_base from the generation), 64-67 and 88-90 (no fallback); PLAN-stage1.md:150-153
findings.problem: The plan says the file is found from /proc/self/maps, 'without it /dev/shm/ + the global segment name', and that the bytes lie 'at 2^44 + the object's offset in the segment + the slot's index, so live objects never share one'. The code has no fallback: without a usable mapping it uses the overflow slot and cannot own the map. It derives the bytes from 26 bits of the random generation, so two live maps share all 257 lock bytes with probability about 2^-26 per pair. Then one map's live holders make the other's slots and claim look held: SEAL_DEAD, or no owner, while they live. The code comments state this choice, but the plan, which reviews and tests are checked against, still describes the old scheme.
findings.evidence: cpp:383-386: '// beyond any segment's end, 4096 bytes per map. Two live maps share bytes with a chance of about 2^-26 per pair' and 'return (1ull << 44) + ((generation >> 1) & ((1ull << 26) - 1)) * 4096;'. cpp:66-67: 'a guessed path could be another file, whose locks nobody else sees'. Plan lines 150-153 as quoted.
findings.suggested_change: Update D8 to describe the generation-derived bytes, their collision chance and its effect (delay only), and the absence of a fallback. Alternatively, derive the bytes from the object's offset in the segment as the plan says, which removes collisions.

findings.title: A process with no segment file (or no free slot) logs at INFO and reparses /proc/self/maps under local_mutex every 100 ms, for good, on the write path
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:397-401, 416-421 (retry every 100 ms), 442-447 (SPDLOG_INFO on every failed scan), 218 / 70-104 (open_segment_file reads all of /proc/self/maps)
findings.problem: When the scan fails (all slots held, or no file: the segment unlinked, '(deleted)', or open failing), the process retries every 100 ms from a BPF write. Each retry takes the process-wide local_mutex, reads and parses the whole of /proc/self/maps when there is no description, and logs 'no writer slot of its own for pid ...' at INFO. That is 10 log lines a second per writing process, never suppressed after the first. Other writer threads of the process that see the retry expire queue on local_mutex behind the parse. CLAUDE.md asks for rate-limited logs on per-event paths, and the plan says 'a write never runs the scan'.
findings.evidence: cpp:443-447: 'e->retry_ns.store(monotonic_ns() + OVERFLOW_RETRY_NS ...); SPDLOG_INFO("device hash map: no writer slot of its own for pid {} (all held, or no segment file); writing in the shared slot", getpid());' runs on every failed scan. For the no-file case, ensure_description (cpp:218) calls open_segment_file again on each retry, under local_mutex (cpp:409).
findings.suggested_change: Log the overflow state once per process per map, or with a doubling back-off. When open_segment_file reports that no file exists, as opposed to all slots being held, stop retrying the open, or back off much longer than 100 ms.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds, and blocker is the right severity. I could not refute it.

**What happens.** A CLONE_VM child with its own fd table runs no fork handler. That covers vfork, glibc posix_spawn's clone(CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK|SIGCHLD), and clone(CLONE_VM) without CLONE_FILES.
- If such a child makes the process's first write to the map, `ensure_description` opens the segment file in the child's own fd table (cpp:218). The child takes slot s's lock through that description (cpp:428).
- It then stores `e->fd` and `e->slot` in `local_maps` (cpp:449). `local_maps` is the parent's memory.
- When the child execs or exits, the description is gone and the kernel frees the lock.
- From then on the parent's fast path (cpp:389-396) returns `&writers[s].count` with no lock behind it. The slow-path recheck at cpp:414 checks only `e->fd >= 0`, not that the parent holds the lock.

**The seal.** It goes wrong once a writer of that process stays in flight past the first `discount_dead_writers` call. That call comes at poll 4096 (cpp:688-690), about 1 ms after the seal starts on this Orin.
- The sealer's own description takes the free lock (cpp:473) and clears the live count (cpp:477-478).
- The next poll reads 0, so `seal()` returns true (cpp:681-682) while a writer that read PHASE 0 still writes the frozen table.
- That writer's `fetch_sub` (cpp:514) then wraps the slot's count to UINT64_MAX. Once PHASE is back at 0, the sum of the counts can wrap to 0 (cpp:279-282, 290-293).
- A writer preempted for a millisecond on a loaded host is enough. A stopped or stuck writer is discounted deterministically, where the plan says it yields SEAL_DEAD.

**Scope.** It needs `e->fd < 0` when the child writes: the process's first write to that map, or a write after `forget_locks` (cpp:209-219, reached from 421). If the parent already holds a description, the child locks through it and the plan's alive-side statement is right (parent-first control below). The finding's claim that "often every write" comes from a spawn child goes further than this precondition; the first write is what matters.

**Reachability.** CLAUDE.md:517-551 and 1219-1220 say vfork and posix_spawn children run hooked calls and programs with no fork handler, for example on execve's entry in syscall-trace mode. The earlier refuter accepted that premise for slots-8 (reread-fixes.json:77, :128). `seal_and_build` and the CPU writers are in this commit; only the agent-side caller of the seal is not built yet.

**Not a stated limit.**
- PLAN-stage1.md:195-196 (D8 limits) lists only "a vfork-style child, which shares its parent's description, killed in flight while the parent lives" (alive side).
- The section 10 row at :1237 says "a vfork child shares its parent's slot (README 10, alive side)".
- RULES-ofd item 6 checked only a lock the parent already held.

So the plan states the opposite of this case, and the test file has no vfork, posix_spawn or CLONE_VM case (grep is empty).

**Consequences (c) and (d).** I reran both.
- (d) The wrapped count hides a well-behaved process's writer from a later seal.
- (c) relies on `set_devhash_usable_writer_slots_for_test(1)` to force the collision. In real use, R would need a matching pid % 256 or a chain of held slots. It supports the finding but does not carry the severity.

**Related but separate.** The reproducer also shows the stale fd number closing a host fd, in a fork child and in the destructor. That is a different defect and is not counted here.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds, and the right severity is blocker, not major.

Three sites call close(e->fd) without checking the number:
- the fork handler (cpp:235-236)
- the destructor (cpp:359-360)
- local_entry when the generation changed (cpp:183-184)

Only ensure_description (cpp:204-213) checks it with fstat. The writer fast path (my_writer_count, cpp:389-403) never re-checks once a slot is cached. So after the host closes the agent's description, the recorded number stays stale indefinitely, and the lowest-free-fd rule hands it to the next file. The plan treats that host close (close_range) as reachable: D8 Limits line 198-199, D11c line 335-339, README 11 line 1007-1010. It only says that the slot and the claim are released; it never says the agent will later close whatever file has that number. Nothing in the plan covers this, and the test at test_gpu_device_hash.cpp:1584-1597 never reuses the number.

What I reproduced myself, against the frozen 84ce9813d libruntime.a:
- With only the documented close_range trigger (no vfork, no hooks), each of the three sites closes a host file at the reused number:
  - the fork child, before any user code runs;
  - the process itself, in the destructor;
  - the process itself, on its first write to a new map the tool created at the old map's address.

The same root cause reaches the blocker list.
- All devhash maps in one segment share one file, so the stale number of map A can be this process's description for map B, opened after the host's close.
- Destroying A here, or a new map at A's address, then closes B's description. That drops B's live slot lock while B's entry still caches the slot.
- A sealer in another process then discounts a B writer that read PHASE 0. seal_and_build returns 1, the key is missing from the image, and the count wraps to 0xffff...ffff.
- The same close drops B's claim, but still_holds_claim() still returns 1, because fstat of the number matches the segment's dev/ino. Another process claims B with first_copy, so there are two owners, with no bound. The plan's D11c fstat check cannot catch this.
- None of this is "a write in flight at that moment" (the plan's stated loss). B's description was opened after the host close, and the agent's own stale close drops it later.

The suggested fix (compare st_dev/st_ino before closing) is not enough. It stops the host-file closes, but it treats another entry's description of the same segment file as a match. A fix needs real description identity. Options:
- one shared, refcounted description per segment per process;
- a marker OFD lock per entry checked with F_OFD_GETLK through e->fd (a description does not conflict with its own lock);
- or never closing a number that has not been proven to be this entry's.

On the hang clause: the finding's hang came through the vfork trigger and the reproducer's own pipe. For the documented trigger alone, whether the host hangs or only gets EBADF depends on the host's code. The blocker rests on the seal and two-owner results above, not on that hang.

The three other close sites call close(e.fd) without checking. After a host close_range (or any close of the agent's fd) followed by its own open/pipe/socket at that number, (a) every glibc fork child closes the host's fd in the child, e.g. a prefork server's listening socket or a pipe end, and the next open in the child takes that number; (b) destroying the map in that process closes the host's fd; (c) a new 1533 map at a destroyed map's address does the same at its first claim or slow write. This breaks the host-safety invariants (fd misuse in the traced process and its children).
findings.evidence: repro.cpp 'fork': P claims A (fd 4), calls close_range(3,~0U,0), and the host pipe gets fds 3 and 4. After fork, the child prints 'host pipe read end fcntl=0 (open), write end fcntl=-1 (Bad file descriptor)' (rc 30). repro.cpp 'dtor': 'destructor: host pipe fds 3 4 after destroy: fcntl 0 -1' (rc 40).
findings.suggested_change: Close only a number that still refers to the entry's file: fstat and compare st_dev/st_ino with e.dev/e.ino, as ensure_description does. Otherwise just forget the number. With claim-1's fix, also prefer checking that the description still holds the entry's locks. Add the fork and destructor cases above as tests (close_range, a host pipe on the old number, fork, check the pipe in the child).

findings.title: After the host closes the description, the writer fast path keeps its cached slot without the lock for good; README 11 / D8 understate the window
findings.problem: The plan states the close_range limit as 'a write in flight at that moment can be missing from the device copy'. In practice my_writer_count never checks the description again; only the slow path does, and the slot stays cached. So every later write of that process uses a slot whose lock nobody holds. At any later seal, discount_dead_writers takes the free lock and zeroes the count of a live writer that read PHASE 0, and the seal returns true while that writer still updates the table. The update returns 0, but the key is missing from the image. The writer's decrement then wraps the count to 2^64-1. From then on, one in-flight writer in any other slot makes the seal's sum read 0 (UINT64_MAX + 1) before any discount runs. Another process may also take that slot and clear the count.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-ofd-review/claim/repro/slotlost.cpp, built against the frozen lib. Child writes once to take its slot, calls close_range(3,199,0), sleeps 1 s, then parks a writer at writer_after_phase_load with ph=0. Output: 'sealer: seal_and_build=1 with the writer still parked; key 77 in image=0', 'writer: update of 77 returned 0 after the seal', 'in-flight sum after the writer finished: 18446744073709551615'.
findings.suggested_change: Either bound the window or state it correctly. Bounding it: give a cached slot a revalidation time, as retry_ns does, and check the description (fstat plus the F_OFD_GETLK pair from claim-1) at most every ~100 ms on the writer path, forgetting the slot when the lock is gone. Make the sum robust to wrap: sum saturating, or treat any count above a sane bound as 'in flight'. Stating it: rewrite D8's limit and README 11 to 'every write of that process after the close, until it takes a slot again', and mention the wrap.

findings.title: The seal's probe description is not closed in fork children: an fd leak per fork during a seal, and a dead sealer's slot lock can stay held by a child
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:657-667 (probe in seal), 473-479 (lock, clear, unlock), 232-238 (fork child handler only walks local_maps)
findings.problem: seal() keeps its own description open for the whole seal, up to the 1 s bound and longer. It is O_CLOEXEC but not in local_maps, so a host fork during the seal leaves the probe fd open in the child (a leaked fd in the host's child). If the sealing process is killed between taking a slot's lock through the probe and the F_UNLCK, a fork child created in that window keeps the shared description and so the slot's lock. The slot then looks alive while the child lives, its leftover count is never discounted, and later seals end in SEAL_DEAD.
findings.evidence: Code: probe is a local (line 659) closed by probe_closer; devhash_fork_child closes only local_maps[i].fd. RULES-ofd item 5b: a child that keeps its copy keeps the lock after the parent is gone.
findings.suggested_change: Register the probe fd (e.g. in a process-local 'transient descriptions' slot under local_mutex) so that devhash_fork_child closes it too, or open it per discount pass instead of for the whole seal.

findings.title: Children made without glibc's fork (raw clone/clone3 without CLONE_VM) keep the parent's descriptions, and so the claim; this limit is not stated
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:241-243 (handler registered through register_fork_handlers only); plan D8 limits 192-199, README 10
findings.problem: The fork handler runs only on glibc fork() (pthread_atfork, or the agent fork hook installed with the main libc). A host child made by syscall(SYS_clone, SIGCHLD, ...) or clone3 without CLONE_VM that does not exec (some runtimes and sandboxes do this) shares every description. After an owner dies, such a child keeps the claim (no takeover while it lives, and it never delivers). It also keeps the dead parent's writer slot, whose leftover count then holds every seal to SEAL_DEAD. The plan lists only vfork-style children as an alive-side limit.
findings.evidence: RULES-ofd item 5b ('child kept its copy: still held after the parent is gone'); the code has no other release path.
findings.suggested_change: Add the raw-clone child to D8's limits and README 10/11, or detect it: e.g. on the claim/slow path compare a cached getpid() with the current one, as the other fork-sensitive caches do, and forget (not close) inherited descriptions.

findings.title: With no segment file to lock, every writing process rescans /proc/self/maps and logs at INFO every 100 ms per map, for good
findings.problem: The 100 ms overflow retry was meant for 'all slots held'. It also fires when ensure_description fails (segment unlinked and recreated, anonymous mapping, no /proc), which will never resolve. Each retry runs open_segment_file (fopen and a parse of the whole /proc/self/maps, thousands of lines in a CUDA process) under local_mutex on a host thread inside a probe. It then logs 'no writer slot of its own ...' at INFO, i.e. about 10 lines/s per process per map with no end. The all-slots-held case logs at the same rate. CLAUDE.md requires rate-limited logs on per-event paths.
findings.evidence: Lines 442-448: retry_ns = now + OVERFLOW_RETRY_NS and SPDLOG_INFO on every scan that ends in the overflow slot; line 421: ensure_description reruns open_segment_file when e.fd < 0.
findings.suggested_change: Cache 'no segment file' for this map's entry with no retry, or back off exponentially. Log once per entry, or rate-limited, instead of on every scan.

findings.title: lock_base differs from the plan; on a 2^-26 collision, one map's owner blocks the other map's claim for as long as it lives
findings.problem: The plan says the bytes are '2^44 + the object's offset in the segment + the slot's index, so live objects never share one'. The code uses the generation's 26 bits times 4096, so two live maps share all their bytes with probability 2^-26 per pair. On a collision, whoever owns map A holds B's owner byte too. Every claim of B returns not_owner, so B has no device copy at all while A's owner lives. The code comment calls this 'the copy delayed, never wrong', but neither the plan nor the README states this limit. The generation scheme is probably deliberate: stale descriptions in other processes would otherwise hold a recycled offset's bytes.
findings.evidence: lock_base(): (1ull << 44) + ((generation >> 1) & ((1ull << 26) - 1)) * 4096. Offsets up to 0x103ffffff100 lock fine on /dev/shm here (checked: F_OFD_SETLK at 2^44, 2^44+(2^26-1)*4096+256 and 2^62 all return 0).
findings.suggested_change: Update D8 to the generation-based layout and state the collision limit in the README, or remove collisions: e.g. 2^44 + offset * 512, with stale descriptions handled by claim-9's cleanup.

findings.title: Descriptions of maps destroyed by another process are never closed in this process
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:135-137 ('entries are never removed'), 350-363 (destructor runs only in the destroying process), 177-188
findings.problem: The destructor closes only the destroying process's own description. Every other process that wrote or claimed the map keeps its fd until it exits, or until a new 1533 map lands at the same address in its own table. A long-running traced process that sees many tool sessions' 1533 maps at different addresses therefore accumulates open fds, up to LOCAL_MAPS-1 = 1023, which is the size of a default RLIMIT_NOFILE soft limit. The stale descriptions also keep a removed segment's file alive and keep their old slot/claim bytes locked.
findings.evidence: forget_locks/close happen only in local_entry's gen-mismatch path, the destructor (this process) and the fork child; nothing walks entries whose object was destroyed elsewhere.
findings.suggested_change: On the slow/claim paths, cheaply drop entries whose object's generation no longer matches what the shm holds at that address (read gen through the object when the address is still mapped), closing them with claim-3's check. Alternatively cap the number of open descriptions per process and state the bound.

findings.title: Nothing gives the claim back when the agent detaches while the process keeps running
findings.file_line: plan PLAN-stage1.md:341-349 (D11d lists only the failure paths); runtime/agent/agent.cpp:448-483 (perform_detach destroys links only); nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:139 (descriptions in static local_maps)
findings.problem: The claim's lock lives in a description held by static local_maps until the process exits, execs or forks. After 'bpftime detach' (or any teardown of the owner's delivery) the process stops delivering but still holds the owner byte. No other process can take the map over while it lives, so the claim is stuck with a holder that does nothing. The plan does not list this path among those that release the claim, nor as a README limit.
findings.evidence: release_claim() is called only from make_image's failure and catch paths; perform_detach calls destroy_all_attach_links and nothing in the 1533 code.
findings.suggested_change: In S5, release every claim this process holds (release_claim) when the delivery for 1533 stops (detach, ctx teardown). Add that to D11d and test it: an owner detaches, and another process's claim gives takeover.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds. I reproduced it independently, built from the commit's own source.

**What the code does.** In 84ce9813d, still_holds_claim() (nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:606-614) returns `ensure_description(*e, this) && e->owner_locked`. ensure_description() (lines 207-220) only checks that fstat(e.fd) gives the segment file's dev and ino. Every 1533 map entry in a process opens its own description of that one file through open_segment_file(), and open() takes the lowest free number. So after a host close_range, one map's reopen can land on another map's stale e.fd. That map's fstat then matches, and its owner_locked=true is believed, although the kernel released its owner byte when the old description was closed. Another process then takes the claim, and the old owner keeps passing the check for as long as the other description stays at that number, which in practice is the process's lifetime.

**This is not covered by a stated limit.** The code follows D11c to the letter, so the error is in the plan's bound. D11c says "both deliver for at most one delivery period". README 11 says "until the old owner's next delivery check (fstat)". D11b rests cross-process exclusion "on the kernel alone". The reproducer shows the check passing three times while another process holds the claim, with no bound. A stated limit that is wrong is still a finding.

**Severity: blocker.** The result is two owners with no time limit. D10 requires one mirror writer at a time, and run_mutex only serializes writers within one process. So two delivering owners would overwrite each other's mirror slots, which is a wrong result.
- Caveat: delivery (S5) is not built at this commit. What this commit shows is the guard returning true while the owner byte is free, and a second process then getting first_copy.

**When it happens.** All three are needed:
1. The host closes the agent's descriptors at run time. The plan treats this as in scope: README 11, and S2.14's close_range case.
2. The owner process has at least two 1533 maps with descriptions in the same segment. Any map the process claimed or wrote has one.
3. A reopen lands on the stale number of an entry that has not been checked yet.

Condition 3 depends on the fd layout but is deterministic for a given layout. Both check orders can trigger it. One layout detects both maps (mode 3 below).

**One overstatement in the finding.** The seal's probe is closed when seal() returns, so the probe route gives only a bounded window. The "no time limit" part rests on another map's description.

**The test.** "an owner whose description the host closed knows it" (test_gpu_device_hash.cpp:1584-1597) uses one map and no reuse. It cannot fail for this.

**The suggested fix.** I did not check it. Its premise, that F_OFD_GETLK does not report the caller's own description's lock, is not among the checked rules in RULES-ofd.md.

Each takes the lowest free fd, and the code never moves the result above 2. The host's own stdio writes then overwrite the Boost managed-segment header.

The exposure is wider than the finding says. Besides claim() and the seal's probe (cpp:659), every CPU writer goes through it: elem_update -> my_writer_count -> slow_writer_count -> ensure_description -> open_segment_file (cpp:416-421). The 1533 map is wired into map_handler.cpp (lines 338, 684, 872, 1082), so this path is live in this commit. It runs in any traced process whose BPF program updates the map.

- The D8 limits (plan 192-199) and D11c (335-339) cover only a host that closes descriptors it does not own, through close_range.
- README items 10-11 (plan ~1000-1010) say the same.
- s2/ofd/RULES-ofd.md and the earlier review JSONs never mention stdio or fd numbers.

Before this commit, bpftime kept no read-write fd on the segment file. Boost 1.83's managed_shared_memory is managed_open_or_create_impl<shared_memory_object, align, true, false>, so StoreDevice=false and the fd closes after mapping. - What it needs is at least two of fds 0-2 free when the description is opened.
- With only fd 2 closed, the segment lands on fd 3 and the host is safe.
- The agent's default log sink is a rotating file opened at bootstrap (bpftime_logger.hpp, agent.cpp:155-159). It takes one low number first. So with the default agent setup, all three of 0-2 must be closed. The segment then lands on fd 2, stderr.
- With BPFTIME_LOG_OUTPUT=console, which the rootless agent sets (rootless_agent_entry.cpp:57-58), or in a process without that log file, two closed numbers are enough.

The precondition is uncommon but legitimate, and CLAUDE.md rule 3 (lines 172-175) says to leave the host's stdin, stdout and stderr untouched. bpftime_shm::open_fake_fd (bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:867-873) already loops until it gets an fd above 2.

The SIGABRT the finding cites (lock_exception -> terminate) comes from the bare Boost test program after.cpp. I did not check whether bpftime's allocation paths catch that exception, so I do not rely on the abort. The hang alone, plus the corrupted shared header, carries blocker.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds, and the severity should be blocker, not major. I reproduced it independently against the frozen 84ce9813d library, and once more without any test knob.

(1) After the host closes a process's description, that process keeps its cached slot with no lock behind it. Two code paths keep it:
- The fast path, my_writer_count (cpp:389-403), never looks at the description again.
- The slow path also returns the cached slot early, at cpp:414-415 (`if (s >= 0 && s < WRITER_SLOTS && e->fd >= 0) return &writers[s].count;`), because e->fd stays at its old value after the host's close. This corrects the finding's "only the slow path does".

The slot is only forgotten through ensure_description (cpp:207-220), which runs from claim(), still_holds_claim(), or a slot of -1 or overflow. So "for good" is literally true for a process that never claims: the tool, the server, or a traced process that only writes. Any later seal's discount_dead_writers (cpp:464-485) takes the free lock and zeroes a live writer's count, and the seal returns true while that writer is still writing.

(2) The plan's limit is worded wrongly, not just tersely. D8 (PLAN-stage1.md:198-199) and README 11 (1006-1009) say "a write in flight at that moment can be missing". In slotlost, a write made 1 s after the close is missing. Section 10's row for slots-1 says "gone" ("a second claimant steals a live slot; count wraps"); with close_range that failure is back. The trigger is the one the plan already acknowledges (a host calling close_range, RULES-ofd item 8), so the orchestrator can weigh that.

(3) It reaches a writer that no limit covers. A process Q whose pid lands on the freed slot takes its lock legitimately and zeroes the count while P's writer is in flight (slow_writer_count, cpp:425-435). P's decrement then wraps the slot to 2^64-1. The seal adds the counts with a plain, wrapping `sum +=` (cpp:281 in sealer_enter, cpp:292 in sealer_poll), so Q's own writer in flight brings the sum to 0. The first seal then returns true at once while Q, a live lock holder whose description was never closed and which read PHASE 0, is still writing. Q's key is missing from the image. That is the blocker definition: a seal returning true while a writer that read PHASE 0 can still write, and a live writer's write missing from the image.

Discount cannot repair the wrapped slot while Q holds the lock. With no writer in flight the sum reads 2^64-1, so seals time out into SEAL_DEAD instead. I did not test the finding's wider claim that "from then on any other slot" is affected. In the slotlost sequence the wrap comes after a seal that already returned true, and a wrapped count on a free lock is cleared by the next discount or the next taker. The harmful, lasting case is a live holder sitting on the wrapped slot, which is what sharewrap shows.

The suggested changes are sound and cheap: check the description on the writer path at most every ~100 ms, and make the sum wrap-proof. verdicts.reason:
One part of the finding is literally true: nothing in 84ce9813d releases the owner byte on detach. release_claim() is called only from make_image's catch and !ok paths, at nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:644 and :648. The plan never names detach. But the delivery and the D11d wiring are S5, which is not built yet, so this is a finding against the plan, not the commit's code.

The finding's premise is wrong. Under the design S5 reuses (1531's deliver_locked, plus the D11a copy cache), the detached owner is not "a holder that does nothing", and detach does not stop delivery.
- The delivery thread stops only at atexit. s.stop is stored only in final_delivery_at_exit (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:554). deliver_now has no callers.
- The per-process copy cache (static `made`, :698) is never cleared.
- perform_detach (agent.cpp:448-483) calls only destroy_all_attach_links and reset_instantiated_state. On the CUDA side, nv_attach_impl::detach_by_id switches the probes off and clears the patched-module state for the next session. It touches neither the copies nor the delivery thread.
- So the detached owner keeps its device copy and keeps delivering it. A later session in the same process takes its own lock again and gets have_copy, reusing that copy (D11a "every later link ... gets the same base"; D11d).

Ownership therefore lasts as long as the process, by design, as for 1531. The plan states that in substance:
- D11c: "Liveness is the lock ... A free owner byte means no live owner".
- README 11 lists the only ways an owner is replaced: it "died, was killed or exec'd".
- README 6 says a process without a copy because of "another owner" never reaches the device map.
- S5 test 2: "a second child gets 0 while the owner holds its claim (alive, or stopped)".

The outcome is fail-safe: the other process gets not_owner, its GPU lookups give NULL and inserts -1, and nothing is wrong or lost.

The suggested change would cause a blocker. It releases the claim "when the delivery for 1533 stops (detach, ctx teardown)". But agent_control runs the same teardown before every re-init (agent.cpp:759-760). Releasing there, while the cache and delivery thread live on, lets process B take over while A keeps delivering: two owners writing the mirror. A's next session would then hit its cached copy and use it without holding the claim. The fix would also have to free the device copy, and the design avoids that because patched modules and the driver may still reference it.

What remains is at most a nit: one README sentence saying a detached owner keeps the map until it exits. That is not the gap the finding describes.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds. ensure_description (cpp:207-220) accepts any descriptor whose fstat matches the segment's dev/ino. still_holds_claim (cpp:606-614) returns `ensure_description(*e, this) && e->owner_locked`, so it never asks whether that description still holds the owner byte's lock.

After the host runs close_range, the agent's next open of the segment file for another 1533 map gets the lowest free number. That is the old owner's number whenever the free numbers below it are the same as at the original open. This is not a race; it follows from lowest-free allocation. Routes that keep the number: slow_writer_count (cpp:421, a first CPU write to another map), claim (cpp:571) and still_holds_claim (cpp:613) on another map. Correction to the finding: the seal probe (cpp:659) is closed when seal() returns, so it matters only if it runs at the same moment.

After that, the old owner's check says yes for as long as the other entry keeps the number open, while another process takes the claim. That makes two owners for an unbounded time, which is a blocker under the rubric.

This is not a stated limit:
- The plan text at commit time (results copy, 22:47; D11c at lines 335-339, limit 11 at 1007-1010) bounds the overlap at "at most one delivery period" by the fstat check. That bound is wrong.
- The current plan file (edited 23:33, after the 22:46 commit) requires the lock to be read from /proc/self/fdinfo, plus a holder hint. D8 lines 175-179 say: "matching the file alone is not enough, because the number may now name another description of the same file". D11c lines 372-374 say the same. The commit has neither: no fdinfo, hint or lock re-check anywhere in the .cpp. So the code does not provide what the plan requires.
- In the current plan, limit 11 (1043-1046) and S2 item 14 (737-739) still name the fstat check, which disagrees with its own D8/D11c.

The test claim also holds. The section at test.cpp:1584-1597 only calls close_range and never reopens the segment file, so it passes against this bug.

Correction to suggested_change: the code already clears the claim on a dev/ino mismatch or EBADF (cpp:216 forget_locks, cpp:170). What is missing is checking that the description actually holds the owner byte's lock.

The finding holds for seal_skips_overflow and major is the right severity. The committed code is correct: seal() at cpp:654 sums WRITER_SLOTS + 1 slots, discount_dead_writers at cpp:468 loops i < WRITER_SLOTS, and the added case R1 passes. That mutant is caught by both R1 and R1b, so the suggested R1 is a valid test for the real gap. Severity stays major, not blocker: this is a missing test guarding a blocker-class property, not a defect in the committed code.

findings.title: A vfork-style child's first write leaves the parent writing in a slot nobody holds, and the parent's entry keeps an fd number that was open only in the child
findings.problem: local_maps lives in process memory. A CLONE_VM child (vfork, posix_spawn, system(), Go os/exec) shares that memory, but it has its own copy of the fd table. If the child makes the process's first write to the map, it opens the description in its own table, takes slot i, and stores slot i and its fd number into the parent's entry. When the child execs or _exits, its table goes, and the lock goes with it. From then on the parent writes in slot i through the fast path and never scans again, so it holds no lock there. The sealer's probe takes the free lock and zeroes the count of a live writer that has already read PHASE 0, and seal() returns true. Another process's scan can also take slot i and zero the count (cpp:432). The plan puts vfork children on the alive side only (D8 line 195, README 10 line 1004). That holds only when the parent took the slot first. Probes do run in such children: runtime/src/producer_identity.cpp:13-19 and text_segment_transformer.cpp note_clone_syscall exist because of them, and execve probes fire in exactly this window.

findings.title: Children made without fork() (glibc clone(), raw SYS_clone) run no fork handlers and keep the owner's claim after it dies
findings.problem: D11b (plan line 331) says 'An owner's fork child closes the inherited description (D8), so it never shares the claim'. That holds only for children made through glibc fork(). A child made with clone(SIGCHLD) shares the owner's description, so after the owner dies the claim stays held while the child lives. Nobody takes over, deliveries stop, and other agents get not_owner. The repo already notes that raw clones skip fork handlers (producer_identity.cpp comment: 'a raw clone(SIGCHLD) or glibc's clone() keep the forking thread's cached ids'). This is a liveness gap that the plan and README 11 do not state.
findings.evidence: fork_handlers.cpp runs handlers only through pthread_atfork and bpftime_agent_fork_hook, both called only by glibc fork(). The claim lock belongs to the description, which the clone child's fd table copy keeps.
findings.suggested_change: State it in README 11, or detect a pid change at the owner's checks (still_holds_claim) and in a child release the inherited description's locks without closing them.

findings.title: local_mutex is held across hookable libc calls outside a callback scope (claim, release_claim, still_holds_claim, destructor), while the writer's slow path blocks on the same non-recursive mutex
findings.problem: Inside BPF callbacks there is no re-entry: attach_callback_scope and the Gum guard stop nested probes. claim(), still_holds_claim() and the destructor, however, run open, fopen, fstat, fcntl and close under local_mutex on whatever thread calls them. If a probe fires on that same thread, the first write to any 1533 map not yet slotted in the process deadlocks on local_mutex, a hang in the traced process. Two ways this happens: a host signal handler during still_holds_claim() on an application thread at a hooked sync (deliveries may run on any thread, D16), or a Frida probe on open/fstat/fcntl in LD_PRELOAD mode. The current agent init paths run under attach_callback_suppression_scope and agent_internal_section (agent.cpp:751, :761), so claim() from the pre-pass is covered. The open risk is S5's delivery-time callers.
findings.evidence: slow_writer_count begins 'std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(local_mutex);'. still_holds_claim holds the same mutex across ensure_description, which calls fstat and possibly open_segment_file (fopen, open, close).
findings.suggested_change: In slow_writer_count use try_lock and fall back to the overflow slot when the mutex is busy, so the writer path never blocks on an agent-internal lock. Alternatively, require S5 to call still_holds_claim and make_image under attach_callback_suppression_scope, and say so in the header.

The finding holds, and it deserves a higher severity than minor. The paths it cites are latent, but the same defect is reachable at 84ce9813d through the fork-child handler, which the finding does not name.

Neither the plan nor the header requires S5 callers to suppress probes. D11c requires still_holds_claim() before each delivery, and the existing deliveries (drain_loop, deliver_in_sync_call on the application thread in AT_SYNC mode, final_delivery_at_exit) carry no suppression or ignore_probes.

(2) Reachable now: devhash_fork_prepare takes local_mutex (:224), and devhash_fork_child calls close() on each inherited description (:236) and then forget_locks (:237), unlocking only at :239. In LD_PRELOAD/Frida mode, atfork handlers run without attach_callback_suppression_scope, and the Frida listener does not filter callers. A uprobe on libc close fires there. probe_grace::enter takes no lock when the forking thread already has a reader; otherwise it blocks on registry_mutex in one handler order, which is also a hang.

Trigger: a probe on libc close whose program writes a 1533 map, where either that map's entry was already reset earlier in the loop (about half the address orders when the process holds two descriptions) or the map has no entry while another description exists, and the host forks. my_writer_count sees slot -1, slow_writer_count locks local_mutex (:409), and the child hangs inside fork(); a parent that waits on it hangs too.

The latent S5 path also fires again later, not only at start-up: the slow path re-runs every 100 ms in the overflow slot and after a lost description. Once one thread is stuck, every later host fork() blocks in devhash_fork_prepare.

Only the writer-side try_lock with an overflow-slot fallback fixes the fork child. The finding's alternative (S5 calls under a suppression scope, stated in the header) does not cover it.
